summary: The note surveys how cryptocurrency is entering local economies in the US in September-October 2023, mixing small-business anecdotes with themes of adoption, volatility, and integration. Business owners are drawn by lower fees and borderless sales but face price swings, technical and compliance hurdles, and rural skepticism. Coping strategies and education initiatives such as peer support networks, hedging products, and workshops are emerging to help.
one_line: Small businesses across the US are cautiously adopting cryptocurrency in late 2023, weighing lower fees and global reach against volatility and integration hurdles.
key_facts: Tom Henderson, a small bakery owner in the suburbs of Illinois, put up a 'Bitcoin Accepted Here' sign around September 12, 2023.
Anna Rodriguez, a florist in Austin, Texas, accepted Bitcoin for a large order and saw its value plummet overnight, likening it to "a 15% discount sale that I never intended to have."
Michael Avery, a financial advisor specializing in small businesses, is increasingly in demand to advise entrepreneurs on digital currencies.
A September 27, 2023 survey by independent market analyst Travis Johnson found businesses adopting cryptocurrencies reported a 20% increase in customers from the digital savvy demographic.
Janet Green, who runs a handicraft store in rural Vermont, resists crypto, saying "People come here for the charm of the old world, not technology."

On October 15, 2023, Eddie Clarkson, owner of a local electronics shop, contacted a software company to set up a crypto payment gateway, noting the heavy back-end work, tax compliance, and cybersecurity needs.
Sally Jenkins, who runs an online homemade jams and preserves store, began accepting cryptocurrency in late September 2023 and avoided currency conversion and international transaction fees.
On September 22, 2023, local business owners in San Diego formed a support network to share crypto experiences and strategies.
One coping method is immediately converting cryptocurrencies into fiat currency to avoid lasting exposure to volatility.
Simon Yates, a local hardware store owner, is exploring cryptohedge products, comparing them to insurance against wild price movements.
The Chamber of Commerce in Nashville, Tennessee launched the Crypto for Commerce workshop series on September 18, 2023, to demystify digital currencies for small business owners.
Adoption is more enthusiastic in tech hubs and metropolitan areas, while rural settings remain skeptical.
